Is it an acne scar or just a mark?
Most of what people call acne scars is colour, not texture - and the two behave very differently.

Brown marks are pigment left behind after a spot, and they are especially common in deeper skin tones. Red or pink marks are also flat, but the colour comes from vessels. A true scar is a change in shape: a dip or dent in the surface.

The simplest check needs a window. Stand side-on to the light: a dent throws a small shadow, a flat mark does not. Then run a finger over it. Flat means colour. A dip means shape.

Marks are rarely quick. In 324 acne patients across seven Asian countries, 58% had brown marks, and for more than half they lasted at least a year - five years or longer for 22.3%. Picking was commonly reported, and it is the one factor fully in your hands.

Dents are a different question. In a separate six-month study, most new dents still present at six months were still there two years later, and spots that lingered longer carried more risk of leaving one. That makes a dent a question for an in-person assessment, not for a product.

If spots are still arriving, they come first. Marks follow spots.

Abad-Casintahan F et al. J Dermatol 2016. doi:10.1111/1346-8138.13263
Tan J et al. J Drugs Dermatol 2017;16(6):566-572
